messages:
sarah: heads up - noticed a handful of KMS keys still list principals that were supposed to be removed by last night's SCIM deprovision job. tagging eng-infra and oncall.
ajay: ugh, when you say "list principals" do you mean IAM bindings or the KMS key grant entries? can you paste the query you used?
sarah: KMS grants. ran `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy` and then grepped for deleted users. saw entries like `user:svc-account+old-extid@example.com` still present.
lee: oh right - we shipped the RBAC subject-name refactor last week (replaced `username`->`external_id` in the provisioner). SCIM deprovisioner still looks up by username.
ajay: that mismatch could explain it. SCIM removed the user record from IDP but the key grant check fails to match so it never removed the grant.
infra-bot: deploy noted: provisioner-service v2.14.0 rolled last Wed 03:12 UTC (includes rbac-subject-refactor)
sarah: timeline: provisioner refactor -> idp exported new `external_id` values -> SCIM job used old lookup -> deprov job marked user removed but skipped KMS grant revocation because principal lookup returned no match.
oncall-jamie: are audit logs showing attempts to revoke? can you dump the deprov job log for that window?
sarah: yes. excerpt:
```
2026-03-18T02:15:09Z deprov: user removed: extid:12345
2026-03-18T02:15:09Z deprov: looking up principal for username: alice
2026-03-18T02:15:09Z deprov: principal not found, skipping kms revoke
```
lee: so deprov thinks username is alice, but IDP only surfaces external_id:12345 now. nasty edge-case.
ajay: quick mitigation: add an interim mapping table for last 7 days in the deprov job to map external_id->username from the export snapshot and run a backfill revoke for any KMS grants with principals matching stale usernames.
lee: agree. also add an alert for stale KMS grants older than 24h after deprovision timestamp.
sarah: started a short script to detect candidates:
```
# list grants that contain '@example.com' AND match known-deprovisioned-usernames
python tools/find_stale_kms_grants.py --since 2026-03-18T00:00Z
```
infra-bot: run initiated by sarah at 2026-03-18T12:03:21Z - results queued
ajay: for long-term fix we should make deprov lookup by both `username` and `external_id` and add a backward-compatibility layer for 30 days. also bump e2e test for KMS revoke to cover subject-name changes.
lee: +1. file a Jira for the refactor remediation and put temporary access control hold on any keys that had grants removed pending verification.
oncall-jamie: i've temporarily disabled cross-project key access for the affected keys and contacted the owners. will escalate if any service impact.
sarah: postmortem notes I'll add: root cause = subject-name field rename in RBAC refactor without ensuring SCIM/deprov compatibility; missing test coverage for KMS grant revocation; detection gap for grant-orphaning.
ajay: action items:
- short-term backfill script run (sarah)
- add compatibility lookup & tests (lee)
- alert for stale grants (ajay)
- Jira for RBAC refactor remediation + add changelog checklist (sarah)
- confirm no active access from orphaned principals (oncall-jamie)
sarah: executing backfill now. will post results.
infra-bot: backfill completed 2026-03-18T12:18:07Z - 6 grants removed, 2 flagged for manual review
sarah: thanks - manual review showed 2 were service accounts that had undergone name-change; removed after owner confirmation.
lee: closing loop: will add compatibility layer and land tests by end of week. also propose we add an audit rule that surfaces any KMS grant where the principal lookup fails during deprov.
ajay: leaning to add an integration test that runs a fake RBAC rename and ensures deprov still revokes KMS grants.
oncall-jamie: good job catching this early. no incident declared but add to next security sync agenda.
sarah: thx everyone :thumbsup:
